# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_10/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_10/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# According to operation_history: JOIN on Postalcode
# Join df0 and df1 on 'Postalcode' column (inner join by default)
df_joined = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="Postalcode", how="inner")

# Reorder and rename columns to match target schema:
# Target schema: ['Postalcode': string, 'Latitude': float, 'Longitude': float, 'Borough': string, 'Neighborhood': string, 'Neighborhood_joined': string]
# Neighborhood_joined is the same as Neighborhood (string copy)

df_joined["Neighborhood_joined"] = df_joined["Neighborhood"]

# Select and reorder columns exactly as target schema
target_df = df_joined[[
    "Postalcode",
    "Latitude",
    "Longitude",
    "Borough",
    "Neighborhood",
    "Neighborhood_joined"
]]

# Ensure correct dtypes according to target schema
target_df["Postalcode"] = target_df["Postalcode"].astype(str)
target_df["Latitude"] = target_df["Latitude"].astype(float)
target_df["Longitude"] = target_df["Longitude"].astype(float)
target_df["Borough"] = target_df["Borough"].astype(str)
target_df["Neighborhood"] = target_df["Neighborhood"].astype(str)
target_df["Neighborhood_joined"] = target_df["Neighborhood_joined"].astype(str)

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_10/target_multisource.csv"
target_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_10/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_10/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on Postalcode (inner join to keep only matching postal codes)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="Postalcode", how="inner")

# The target schema is:
# ['Postalcode': string, 'Latitude': float, 'Longitude': float, 'Borough': string, 'Neighborhood': string, 'Neighborhood_joined': string]
# The target examples show that Neighborhood_joined is the same as Neighborhood

# Add Neighborhood_joined column as a copy of Neighborhood
joined["Neighborhood_joined"] = joined["Neighborhood"]

# Group by Postalcode, Borough, Neighborhood to ensure uniqueness and preserve key constraints
# Aggregate Latitude and Longitude by taking the first value (since FD says Neighborhood -> Latitude, Postalcode)
grouped = joined.groupby(["Postalcode", "Borough", "Neighborhood"], as_index=False).agg({
    "Latitude": "first",
    "Longitude": "first"
})

# Add Neighborhood_joined column again after groupby (since it was lost)
grouped["Neighborhood_joined"] = grouped["Neighborhood"]

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final_df = grouped[["Postalcode", "Latitude", "Longitude", "Borough", "Neighborhood", "Neighborhood_joined"]]

# Write to output CSV
final_df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_10/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
